note: Facet Bot Blocker is a kernel REQUEST subscriber (priority 101) that blocks a request when isset($_GET['f'][$limit]) — i.e. the f[] facet query array reaches the configured depth — returning 403 (or 410 Gone if facet_bot_blocker_return_gone). Config object facet_bot_blocker.settings has keys facets_bot_blocker_limit (int, default 1), facet_bot_blocker_return_gone (bool), facet_bot_blocker_html (string). NO config ships by default and there is no schema, so get() is null until saved. Three permissions: administer facet bot blocker, access facet bot blocker dashboard, bypass facet bot blocker. Dashboard counters only populate with Memcache/Redis. Cases are grounded in that config object and behaviour.

evals.prompt: How does the facet_bot_blocker module decide to block a request, which query parameter does it look at, and what HTTP status codes can it return?
evals.expected_output: A kernel REQUEST subscriber blocks when the request's f[] facet query array reaches the configured depth (isset($_GET['f'][$limit])). It returns HTTP 403 Forbidden by default, or 410 Gone when facet_bot_blocker_return_gone is enabled.

evals.prompt: In facet_bot_blocker, what is the config object and the setting key that controls how deep the facet parameters can go before a request is blocked, and at what admin path is it configured?
evals.expected_output: The config object is facet_bot_blocker.settings and the key is facets_bot_blocker_limit (integer, default 1). It is configured at /admin/config/system/facet-bot-blocker (route facet_bot_blocker.settings_form).

evals.prompt: Which facet_bot_blocker permission lets a user keep browsing deep faceted URLs without ever being blocked?
evals.expected_output: The 'bypass facet bot blocker' permission — a user who has it is returned early from the event subscriber and is never blocked, whatever the facet depth.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, facet_bot_blocker has been configured. Inspect the live configuration and state the facet parameter depth limit that is currently set.
evals.expected_output: facet_bot_blocker.settings.facets_bot_blocker_limit is 3 on this site, so a request is blocked once it carries f[3].

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, when facet_bot_blocker blocks an over-limit facet request, what HTTP status code does it return? Inspect the live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: facet_bot_blocker.settings.facet_bot_blocker_return_gone is TRUE on this site, so blocked requests return HTTP 410 Gone (not the default 403 Forbidden).

evals.prompt: Configure facet_bot_blocker on this site so that a request is blocked once it reaches the third facet parameter (f[2]) and so that blocked requests return HTTP 410 Gone instead of 403. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: facet_bot_blocker.settings has facets_bot_blocker_limit = 2 and facet_bot_blocker_return_gone = true (e.g. via drush cset facet_bot_blocker.settings facets_bot_blocker_limit 2 and facet_bot_blocker_return_gone 1).

evals.prompt: I run a Drupal site with the Facet Bot Blocker module. When it blocks a bot I want the page to say exactly 'FBB blocked you' instead of the default text. Please set that up.
evals.expected_output: facet_bot_blocker.settings.facet_bot_blocker_html is set to a value containing 'FBB blocked you' (the custom blocked message key).
